question: In a Maths quiz 10 students scored 20 marks, six students scored 19 marks, five students scored 18 marks, four students scored 17 marks, and two students scored 12 marks. The average marks scored by the class (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the Net Deviation Method by taking an Assumed Average = 18.

Net deviation = (10 × 2) + (6 × 1) + (5 × 0) + (4 × −1) + (2 × −6)

Net deviation = 20 + 6 + 0 − 4 − 12 = +10 marks

Average change per student = +10 ÷ 27 ≈ +0.37

Actual Average = 18 + 0.37 = 18.37

**∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.**
